description: The deterministic projection from the selected XNA contract to Common Lisp. tools/api-compat/verify.py applies these rules to the live image; docs/common-lisp-mapping.md is the prose that explains them.

naming.identifier: A CLR identifier becomes a Lisp symbol by inserting a hyphen at each word boundary and lowercasing. Texture2D becomes texture-2d.
naming.reference_type_member: <member>, in the type's package, as a generic function or reader.
naming.value_type_member: <type>-<member>, in the type's package. The prefix is what keeps Rectangle's Left from colliding with Viewport's.
naming.static_class_member: <class>-<member>, so that Mouse and GamePad can join Keyboard's namespace without collision.
naming.constructor: make-instance for a reference type; make-<type> for a value type.
naming.enum_member: a keyword named by the identifier rule; the exact value is preserved in the runtime table.

universal_not_applicable.name: ToString
universal_not_applicable.reason: CLR object printing. A Common Lisp object prints through PRINT-OBJECT, which is a method on a standard generic function rather than a named member of the projected type.

universal_not_applicable.name: GetHashCode
universal_not_applicable.reason: The CLR hash code is not observable through a Common Lisp API; hashing here is SXHASH over the projected value.

universal_not_applicable.name: Finalize
universal_not_applicable.reason: CNA-Lisp has no finalizer that touches a native resource, by design. See docs/ownership-and-lifetimes.md.

universal_not_applicable.name: op_Inequality
universal_not_applicable.reason: Common Lisp has no operator overloading. Inequality is the negation of the projected equality predicate.

OnExiting(Object,EventArgs).reason: The CLR event-handler pattern passes a sender and an argument object. A CLOS method on the game needs neither: the game is the receiver, and the exiting notification carries nothing else.

not_applicable.Dispose(Boolean): The protected dispose(bool disposing) pattern exists to tell a finalizer call from an explicit one. CNA-Lisp has no finalizer that touches a native resource, so there is nothing for the flag to distinguish.

unimplemented.ShowMissingRequirementMessage(Exception): Needs the CLR exception projection and a platform message box.

not_applicable.Dispose(Boolean): The protected dispose(bool) pattern; see Game.Dispose(Boolean).

not_applicable.Equals(Object): There is no universal Object to compare against.

unimplemented.new(Single,Single,Single): The float constructors need Vector3/Vector4 clamping semantics that are not projected yet.

Multiply.reason: One projection; the operator and the named method are the same operation.

Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Color.predefined_value_reason: XNA's 141 predefined colours are static properties on a value type. They are reached here by keyword through PREDEFINED-COLOR, which the generated table makes exhaustive; the thirteen with a named function of their own are declared extensions. A Lisp constant would be wrong for all of them, because Color is mutable and every read of the original is a copy.

Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.Graphic.reason: GraphicsResource's disposal contract, its Name, Tag and Disposing event need the event projection and the GraphicsDevice back-reference, neither of which is in Foundation 1. Texture2D and SpriteBatch carry CNA-Lisp's own disposal instead.

Viewport.reason: The reader is present. The setter is externally blocked: cna_graphics_device_set_viewport takes CNA_Viewport (24 bytes) by value, which the System V AMD64 ABI classifies MEMORY and CFFI cannot pass without cffi-libffi. See docs/native-abi.md.

unimplemented.Present(Rectangle],Rectangle],IntPtr): Needs Nullable<Rectangle> and IntPtr, neither of which is projected.

Present.reason: Only the no-argument overload is projected.

unimplemented.new(Rectangle): The rectangle constructor is not projected; the four-integer one is.

Format.reason: A member whose projected name would be a Common Lisp standard symbol takes an -of suffix: cl:format is inherited into this package.

unimplemented.new(GraphicsDevice,Int32,Int32): Creating an empty texture is not projected in this milestone.
unimplemented.FromStream(GraphicsDevice,Stream,Int32,I: Needs the System.IO.Stream projection. TEXTURE-2D-FROM-PNG-BYTES and TEXTURE-2D-FROM-PNG-FILE are CNA-Lisp additions over the same CNA route, and are declared as extensions rather than claimed as this member.
unimplemented.SetData(!!0[]): Pixel access is not projected in this milestone.

unimplemented.Begin(SpriteSortMode,BlendState,SamplerS: Needs the four graphics state objects.
Needs the state objects and Effect.
Needs the state objects, Effect and Matrix.

Begin.reason: Only the no-argument overload is projected; the state-bearing ones need types this milestone does not have.

Draw.reason: All seven texture overloads are one generic function with keyword arguments. They differ only in which optional parameters are present and in whether the destination is a position or a rectangle, and DRAW-TEXTURE refuses both at once rather than guessing. Text drawing will be a separate generic function when SpriteFont arrives, because one DRAW would then be ambiguous.

Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.Surface.extra_enum_reason: CNA's own renderer-specific surface formats. They are not XNA members; a texture CNA created can report one, so the projection must be able to name it, and a consumer never has to supply one.

GetState.reason: The player-slot overload is an optional argument: the lambda lists differ only by a trailing parameter, so one function expresses both without ambiguity.

IsKeyDown(Keys).reason: The value-type prefix is dropped here: the three query methods read as sentences at the call site and their names are unique in this namespace. Declared rather than assumed.

Item.reason: The CLR indexer. Common Lisp has no indexer syntax, so it projects to a named reader.

Microsoft.Xna.Framework.MathHelper.constant_field_reason: A constant field of a static class projects to a Common Lisp constant, which by convention wears earmuffs: +math-helper-pi+.

Normalize(Vector3).reason: The instance Normalize mutates and the static one answers a new vector. One Lisp function cannot be both without the caller having to know which it got, so the static overload takes the adjective.
